segments.text:
Goal: Sort a sequence of numbers into monotonically
increasing order.
Complexity: Time roughly c1·n² for n items (proportional to
n²).
Key insight: Insertion sort typically has a smaller constant
factor than merge sort.

Goal: Sort a sequence of numbers into monotonically
increasing order. Complexity: Time roughly c2·n·lg n (proportional to n·lg n,
where lg n = log⇔ n). Key insight: Merge sort’s advantage of lg n versus n more
than compensates for difference in constant factors once n
becomes large enough.

Crossover point: No matter how much smaller c⇔ is than c⇔,
there is always a crossover point beyond which merge sort is
faster.

Problem types: (1) Problems with many candidate solutions,
most of which do not solve the problem at hand; (2) Problems
with practical applications (shortest path, topological
sorting, etc.). Algorithm types: Correct vs. incorrect algorithms
(controllable error rate).

Computational models: Sequential (RAM model) vs. parallel
(multicore, task-parallel) vs. online. Computing technology components: Hardware design, GUIs,
object-oriented systems, web technologies, networking,
machine learning — all rely on algorithms at their core.
